title: result["unwrap"]() is the same retired spelling as result.unwrap()
notes: 19-retired-syntax/result-dot-unwrap-is-retired pins the dotted spelling: `Result.unwrap()` is a retired source spelling, not a second propagation operator (postfix `!` replaced it). A literal element access is the same member access as the dotted spelling: same resolved property symbol, same emitted call. A recognizer that tests only for a PropertyAccessExpression is recognition-by-syntactic-form, and the computed spelling escapes every rule it owns. REVIEW-fable-1.md F4 measured `Clock["context"]()` compiling and PANICKING AT RUNTIME on BOTH backends, which is why only a specification-derived case can hold this closed: the differential oracle is structurally blind to a defect the two implementations share. Before the fix this spelling reported SMITHERS1301 — a Result that is never consumed — which is a true statement about a program whose real defect is that it uses retired syntax, and it is the wrong diagnostic to hand the author.
